license.payload: Public domain. Paul Klee died in 1940; his writings and drawings are free in every country that counts the author's life and seventy years, and both works were first published before 1931, so their United States term has run. László Moholy-Nagy, who designed the Skizzenbuch's cover and typography, died in 1946; that term has run too. The Skizzenbuch scan carries the Public Domain Mark 1.0 at the file (Internet Archive, licenseurl). The Tribüne volume is the University of Michigan copy digitized by Google: HathiTrust records the Michigan run of volumes 12–17 (1920) as pdus, public domain in the United States, full view; the Archive item carries no licence of its own. The volume's other contributors (Benn, Becher, Unruh, Felixmüller and others) are held under the same United States term, the archive's jurisdiction; some of their terms still run in Europe.

scope: Held: the Pädagogisches Skizzenbuch whole, in the Bauhausbücher first printing of 1925 (Albert Langen, Munich; cover and typography by Moholy-Nagy), its figures in the scan; and the Schöpferische Konfession of 1920 in the volume that first printed it, the eighteen confessions of Tribüne der Kunst und Zeit XIII (Schickele, Pechstein, Unruh, Großmann, Klee, Toller, Benn, Hoetger, Beckmann, Scharff, Becher, Schönberg, Kaiser, Felixmüller, Sternheim, Hölzel, Marc, Däubler) bound with Bände 12 and 14–17. Not held, as the twenty-eighth seating declared them: the Jena lecture Über die moderne Kunst (1924, first printed 1945); the notebooks as Spiller edited them (Das bildnerische Denken, 1956) and the diaries as Felix Klee edited them (1957), whose editors' apparatus runs under its own terms; and the pictures, whose photographs carry their holders' claims. The Bauhaus lecture manuscripts (Bildnerische Form- und Gestaltungslehre) are digitized by the Zentrum Paul Klee; queued until a file-level licence is verified.
verified_loci: Pädagogisches Skizzenbuch, I.1, the first sentence — 'Eine aktive Linie, die sich frei ergeht, ein Spaziergang um seiner selbst willen, ohne Ziel.'
Pädagogisches Skizzenbuch, the agent of the line — 'Das agens ist ein Punkt, der sich verschiebt'
Pädagogisches Skizzenbuch, the eye's paths through the work — 'Das Auge begeht die ihm im Werk eingerichteten Wege.'
Pädagogisches Skizzenbuch, the water wheel and hammer — 'Das Räderwerk (medial)'
Schöpferische Konfession, I, the first sentence — 'Kunst gibt nicht das Sichtbare wieder, sondern macht sichtbar' (the OCR reads 'sichtbar*', the asterisk the scan's)
why_seated: Klee was declared wanted in the twenty-eighth seating for a reason of his own: too many files and too many image copyright landmines. The Skizzenbuch carries its drawings in the book Klee made of them, under a licence stated at the file, and the Konfession stands in the volume where it was first set beside seventeen other confessions of its moment. Seated with the exact sciences, the line that walks for its own sake stands beside the line Euclid defines as breadthless length.
ruling: Lee Sharks, 2026-10-30: "and then an ea-corpora seating... Einstein, Gödel, Tesla, Copernicus, Galileo, classical Arabic mathematicians... what is in the public domain, and what else? and just to be perverse lets seat the promised Klee notebooks with them"; to the proposed set, "yes, thats a good set".
queued: Paul Klee, Bildnerische Form- und Gestaltungslehre (the Bauhaus lecture manuscripts, 1921–1931), digitized by the Zentrum Paul Klee, Bern: queued until a licence is verified at the file.
Paul Klee, Über die moderne Kunst (the Jena lecture of 1924, first printed Bern: Benteli, 1945): in the United States its term may have been restored; held as the twenty-eighth seating declared it.

declared_2026_10_27.scope: Declared, not seated: Paul Klee, Schöpferische Konfession, in Tribüne der Kunst und Zeit XIII (Erich Reiss, 1920), opens: open (published before 1931); Paul Klee, Pädagogisches Skizzenbuch (Bauhausbücher 2) (Albert Langen, 1925), opens: open (published before 1931); Paul Klee, Über die moderne Kunst (the Jena lecture of 1924) (Benteli, 1945), opens: 1 January 2041 in the United States, if its term was restored; Paul Klee, ed. Jürg Spiller, Das bildnerische Denken (Benno Schwabe, 1956), opens: the editor's apparatus under its own terms; Paul Klee, ed. Felix Klee, Tagebücher 1898–1918 (DuMont Schauberg, 1957), opens: the editor's apparatus under its own terms; Paul Klee, the pictures (about ten thousand works, 1883–1940), opens: the works open; the photographs under their holders' terms. Wanted, and open: the Pädagogisches Skizzenbuch (1925) and the Schöpferische Konfession (1920) in their first printings, with their drawings, from a scan whose licence is verified at the file. The pictures wait on a source whose images carry an open licence of their own.

declared_2026_10_27.why_seated: MANUS, 27 October 2026, after the twenty-seventh seating entered Deleuze and Guattari as a declared absence: "and a declared absence/ wanted seating: hypatia, d & g, pkd, allen ginsberg, anne carson, and tao lin - including the mandalas. and paul klee. too many files and too many image copyright landmines." Paul Klee (1879–1940) is entered as wanted for a reason of his own: "too many files and too many image copyright landmines." His work runs to some ten thousand pictures, scattered across collections whose reproductions carry their own claims, and the shelf takes no file whose licence cannot be verified at the file.
